# Results — Study 633 (BTC Vol Targeting)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**"Bitcoin at a constant 30% vol target: same ride, half the heart attacks — the overlay that
tames the −83% drawdowns"** — rebuilt honestly on daily BTC-USD:
`weight = min(1.5, target_vol / RV_30d)`, daily rebalance, **exactly one execution lag**
(the weight for day *t* uses only returns through the close of day *t−1*). Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month at build time 2026-07-03; the sample
is pinned and never creeps). Fingerprint `9529d5277775`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily BTC-USD closes (public, no key) — price-only **== total-return** (no distributions) |
| Window | 2014-09-17 → 2026-06-30 (**4,305** daily closes, **11.8** years, calendar-daily bars, ann = **365**) |
| Rule | `w_t = min(1.5, 0.30 / RV(30d)_{t−1})`, daily rebalance; grid over targets {20/30/50%} × windows {20/30/60d} |
| Execution | **one lag**: the trailing-vol estimate through close *t−1* sets the weight earning day *t*'s return (`shift(1)`) |
| Cash / rf | un-invested fraction earns **0%** (stablecoin/exchange balance — documented, conservative *against* the overlay); Sharpe races are excess-vs-excess with the same rf = 0 on both legs |
| Costs | one-way bps × \|Δw\| × NAV per daily rebalance (entry trade excluded, both legs pay it); leverage above 1× pays a retail **borrow spread** on max(w−1, 0). Sweep: 0 / 5 / 10+2% / 20+5% |
| Survivorship | single-asset study — no panel survivorship; note that **BTC is itself the surviving coin** of its asset class, so all levels are conditional on that survival |

## Headline race — 30% target, 30d window, cap 1.5×, gross

| leg | CAGR | ann vol | Sharpe | max DD | terminal wealth |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **vol-targeted** | **+38.12%** | **35.54%** | **1.087** | **−52.90%** | **×43.9** |
| buy & hold | +53.63% | 66.50% | 0.981 | −83.40% | ×152.6 |

Sample 4,274 days; average weight **0.604**, levered (w > 1) **10.1%** of days (at the 1.5× cap
1.1%); turnover **6.97× NAV/yr**.

- **Log-wealth growth gap** (strat − B&H): **−10.64 log-pp/yr**, HAC (Newey-West) *t* = **−1.00**
  — the realized growth give-up is large but *not statistically distinguishable* from zero on a
  tape this noisy.
- **HAC alpha** (strategy-on-B&H daily regression): **+7.18%/yr**, *t* = **+1.42**, β = 0.482,
  appraisal 0.468 — positive, **below the t ≥ 2 bar**.

## Does it deliver the promised constant vol? (the mechanical half — yes)

Rolling 30d realized vol of the **strategy**: median **31.0%** (target 30%), p10–p90
**22.4%–47.0%**, inside the 20–40% band **72.8%** of days. Buy & hold: median **54.4%**, p90
**95.1%**. The thermostat works.

## The heart-attack ledger — max drawdown inside each crash window

| window | vol-targeted | buy & hold |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2018 bear | **−52.61%** | −83.40% |
| COVID 2020 | **−31.95%** | −51.86% |
| 2021–22 bear | **−52.86%** | −76.63% |
| **full sample** | **−52.90%** | **−83.40%** |

And the shield is **timing, not just holding less**: against 200 shuffled-vol placebos (same
weight distribution, no alignment with tomorrow's risk) the placebo mean max DD is **−67.34%**
and only **2/200** shuffles reach a drawdown as shallow as the observed −52.90% —
**p = 0.010**. That clears the desk bar on the real tape.

Two robust patterns: the **drawdown cut is parameter-robust** (every cell beats −83.40%, scaling
smoothly with the target), while the **alpha is never certified** anywhere on the grid
(*t* = 0.44–1.48; the Sharpe edge is +0.02…+0.11 and even fades at the 50%/20d corner).
Growth-gap *t* is negative in all nine cells (−0.27…−1.66) — never significant, always a give-up.

## Costs & whipsaw — the overlay is cheap to run

Turnover 6.97× NAV/yr; one-way bps × \|Δw\| daily + retail borrow spread on the levered fraction.

| one-way cost + borrow | Sharpe | CAGR | max DD | alpha (HAC *t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | 1.087 | +38.12% | −52.90% | +7.18%/yr (+1.42) |
| 5 bps | 1.077 | +37.64% | −53.04% | +6.83%/yr (+1.35) |
| 10 bps + 2% borrow | 1.066 | +37.10% | −53.19% | +6.44%/yr (+1.27) |
| 20 bps + 5% borrow | 1.045 | +36.07% | −53.49% | +5.68%/yr (+1.13) |

Costs never flip anything: the drawdown shield and the Sharpe edge both survive 20 bps + 5%
borrow essentially intact (the strategy is mostly *under*-invested, so borrow rarely bites). What
fails the bar gross (**alpha *t* = 1.42**) also fails it net.

## Placebo — shuffled vol signal, 200 seeds (same exposure, no timing)

| quantity | observed | placebo (200 shuffles) | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| HAC alpha | **+7.18%/yr** (*t* = +1.42) | mean +0.23%/yr (mean *t* +0.06 ± 0.97) | **0.105** |
| max drawdown | **−52.90%** | mean −67.34% | **0.010** |

The two halves of the claim split cleanly: the **drawdown shield is genuine timing**
(p = 0.010 — same-distribution random weights can't reproduce it), while the **alpha is not
certified** (p = 0.105 — one shuffle in ten does as well).

## Third axis — "same ride"? The CAGR give-up

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| CAGR give-up (B&H − strat) | **15.51 pp/yr** (+38.12% vs +53.63%) — **71.1%** of B&H CAGR kept |
| terminal wealth | **×43.9 vs ×152.6** — the overlay finishes with **28.8%** of B&H wealth |
| log-growth gap | −10.64 log-pp/yr, HAC *t* = **−1.00** (noise-compatible, arithmetically decisive on the realized path) |
| what it bought | max DD −52.90% vs −83.40%; vol 35.5% vs 66.5% |

**"Same ride" is busted on the realized tape.** +38%/yr is still a fabulous ride in absolute
terms, but it is *not the same ride*: over 11.8 years the vol-targeted investor ends with **less
than a third** of the buy-and-hold wealth. (Honesty note: the growth gap's HAC *t* is only −1.00
— on a tape this volatile the give-up cannot be *statistically certified* either; what is certain
is the realized arithmetic.)

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful (20 seeds per world)

| world | mean alpha | mean HAC *t* | share *t* ≥ 2 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| NULL — risk priced (μ_t ∝ σ_t²) | +0.21%/yr | +0.02 ± 0.69 | 0% |
| PLANTED — leverage effect (mean falls as variance rises) | +27.02%/yr | **+4.33 ± 0.75** | **100%** |

With risk fully priced the overlay earns nothing (it must not); with a planted vol-return
disconnect it lights up on every seed. The harness can bank the effect when it exists — so the
real-tape *t* = 1.42 is a property of the tape, not of the machinery. *(A faithful-engine / power
check only — never cited in support of a stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED (Real on the heart attacks · Weak on the ride).** The drawdown-taming half is
  **real on the real tape**: full-sample max DD **−52.90% vs −83.40%**, robust across all nine
  grid cells, and certified as *timing* by the shuffled-signal placebo (**p = 0.010**, 200
  seeds). The return half is **not**: HAC alpha **+7.18%/yr at t = 1.42** (placebo p = 0.105),
  never above *t* = 2 anywhere on the grid, Sharpe edge a thin +0.02…+0.11. Single-asset study;
  BTC is itself the surviving coin — named.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Mechanically the overlay is as deployable as it gets — turnover
  6.97× NAV/yr costs ~0.5%/yr at 10 bps, BTC capacity is huge, any retail exchange can run it,
  and every number survives 20 bps + 5% borrow. But the thing that survives certification is
  **risk control, not excess return**: you deploy it knowing you gave up **15.5 pp/yr of
  realized CAGR** for the smoother path, and the uncertified Sharpe edge rests on one 11.8-year
  survivor tape. A real shield, not a certified edge — FRAGILE, not INVESTABLE.
- **"Same ride"? — BUSTED.** ×43.9 vs ×152.6 terminal wealth (28.8% kept); the realized CAGR
  give-up is 15.51 pp/yr. Half the heart attacks: **confirmed** (−53% vs −83%, and vol 35.5% vs
  66.5% — the "half" is almost literal). Same ride: **no.**
